input.summary: The England defender drove his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph near his Cheshire home, a court hears
input.evidence_text: Footballer John Stones has been convicted of speeding after he missed a police letter while at the World Cup with England The 32-year-old defender, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan in the summer, was caught driving his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph (69 km/h) along a 30 mph (48 km/h) stretch of a country lane near his Cheshire home in May Stones admitted being the driver when first contacted by Cheshire Police, but did not respond to a second letter offering him the chance to pay a fixed penalty to keep the speeding offence out of court He wrote to Warrington Magistrates Court to explain he had been abroad but was landed with a £1,052 court bill. title: Salford Royal surgery unit fails to improve rating

input.lead: Inspectors said patients were treated with kindness and compassion, but a range of concerns remained
input.summary: Inspectors said patients were treated with kindness and compassion, but a range of concerns remained
input.evidence_text: Surgery services at a Greater Manchester hospital have been rated as requiring improvement after an inspection found further work was needed to ensure patients received safe and timely care The Care Quality Commission (CQC) found Salford Royal Hospital had made enough progress to comply with a warning notice issued in October 2025 over staffing levels and risk management, but identified 12 breaches of regulations relating to patient safety, governance and staffing The inspection was carried out in May following concerns about staffing, governance and safety processes in gynaecology, spinal surgery and neurosurgery Karen Coverley, deputy chief nursing officer, said the trust was pleased inspectors had recognised improvements Inspectors said some staff had not completed life-support training relevant to their roles, infection-control standards remained below trust targets and incidents were not always investigated in a timely manner The report also highlighted concerns over waiting times, discharge delays and patient readmission rates following surgery

title: G20 summit a 'vast policing operation', GMP chief says

input.lead: Sir Stephen Watson says next year's summit will be a 'vast' operation for Greater Manchester Police
input.summary: Sir Stephen Watson says next year's summit will be a 'vast' operation for Greater Manchester Police
input.evidence_text: Greater Manchester's chief constable said hosting the G20 summit in 2027 will be a "vast policing operation" that will put pressure on resources Speaking to BBC Radio Manchester's Hotseat programme , Sir Stephen Watson said the event would "bring pressures" and added: "If we're not careful, it could sadly bend us out of shape." He said the international gathering would provide an opportunity to showcase the city on the world stage, but require a significant commitment of officers and resources Despite the scale of the operation, Sir Stephen said he was confident Greater Manchester Police and forces from across the UK would be able to deliver a successful security operation The G20 summit, an annual gathering of the world's biggest economies, will take place on 27 and 28 November 2027 at the Manchester Central Convention Centre It will be the largest summit ever held in the city and is expected to bring world leaders and their delegations to Manchester, along with thousands of journalists, officials, campaigners and protesters

title: Gun violence falls as shootings down by 77% in Greater Manchester

input.lead: There were 16 firearms discharges in the 12 months to April 2026, compared with 71 incidents in 2020-21
input.summary: There were 16 firearms discharges in the 12 months to April 2026, compared with 71 incidents in 2020-21
input.evidence_text: Gun violence falls as shootings down by 77% in Greater Manchester - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Many of the firearms recovered by Greater Manchester Police were converted from blank-firing weapons. By Richard Stead North West Published 29 September 2026 Shootings in Greater Manchester have fallen by more than three-quarters in the past five years, police figures show. According to Greater Manchester Police (GMP) figures, there were 16 firearms discharges in the 12 months to April 2026, down from 71 in 2020-21, a fall of 77.5% over five years. The force has also recovered more than 420 viable weapons since April 2021. It comes as Greater Manchester marks three-and-a-half years without a fatal shooting in the region. Det Supt Joe Harrop, head of serious and organised crime at GMP, said retaliatory shootings between rival groups had become less common because of the force's "robust police response". Firearms discharges fall In 2008, there were 146 shootings in Greater Manchester. This number had more than halved by 2020. Since then, firearms discharges across the region have continued to fall - albeit not consistently - and GMP data shows there has been a significant drop-off in gun violence rates betweens 2020 and 2026. title: Body building products seized in raids in Rochdale and Manchester

input.lead: Up to a million tablets were confiscated during the raids on a suspects organised crime group
input.summary: Up to a million tablets were confiscated during the raids on a suspects organised crime group
input.evidence_text: Four people have been arrested after police seized what they believe could be up to one million illicit pharmaceutical drugs during raids linked to an organised crime group Three arrests were made at four addresses in Rochdale following a six-month investigation. A fourth person was arrested in Manchester Officers suspect the group was distributing drugs including diazepam, bodybuilding products and weight-loss medications across the UK Det Insp Rich McCorry said there were "serious dangers" associated with unlicensed drugs being sold to the public Two men aged 23 and 52 were arrested at an address on Twingate in Rochdale. A 51-year-old man was arrested on Whittaker Lane in the town, while a 44-year-old man was arrested on Kingsway in Manchester All four were arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to supply Class A, B and C drugs and remain in custody

title: 'The mystery we all want solved': what's with all the corn on Market Street?

input.lead: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred van
input.summary: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred van
input.evidence_text: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred vans, and the doors swing open. Out from within comes cart after cart full of corn This is the not-entirely-secret HQ of the Market Street corn vendors: a four-storey council-owned car park, sitting across two of Manchester’s busiest streets. When I get there, the men are working in silence, hands sheathed in black gloves, bags of sweetcorn torn open, cardboard Just as I’m about to approach a vendor, I’m forwarded an email from a reader. It has the subject line The Mystery We All Want Solved "The reason I’m writing is because the people of Manchester are desperate to know what the hell is going on with all of the corn sellers on Market St "Why are there now so many of them? How on earth do they make a profit? Are they independent vendors or all part of the same company? Is their presence legal? What does their proliferation say about the state of the city centre?”

title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

input.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
input.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
input.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

input.summary: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
